$comment: THE machine-readable Flash plugin protocol contract — the single source of truth for version, deadlines, quotas, error strings, the capability registry and transport limits. Normativity order: this file > docs/plugin-protocol.md prose > any implementation. Swift asserts its constants equal this file (PluginProtocolParityTests); the Rust SDK asserts its transport limits against it (wire.rs) and pins the behaviour in its runtime tests and probe crate. Changing anything here is a protocol change: update the host, SDK, affected plugins, tests, and docs in the same commit (repo rule 7 — no compatibility shims, no version bump while Flash has no external users).

deadlines_ms.$comment: One deadline table. startup: initialize must be answered immediately (no warm-catalog wait; config [plugins] startup_timeout tunes it). query: per-keystroke evaluate. hints: activation hint pull; it blocks the AX queue ahead of the prepared model, so it is a fixed latency ceiling. text_grid: the letter-search grid pull, asked asynchronously only when the focused app publishes no Accessibility text; the search waits on it, so it shares the hints ceiling. perform: all three kinds. ping: reply budget for the idle-liveness probe (sent only after idle_before_ping_ms of inbound silence with no request in flight; ONE miss tears down). shutdown_grace: stdin-close -> SIGTERM; +500ms -> SIGKILL.

host_to_plugin.initialize: request {protocol_version} -> {ok, protocol_version}; reply immediately, once ever; ok:false or a version mismatch is terminal (flush, exit 0)
host_to_plugin.event: notification {name, payload}; never replied; `core:poll:<name>` ticks a cadence registered through `poll` and bypasses `listen`; `core:status.observed` carries {segments: [name]}, the complete set of unique nonempty manifest `status` names of this plugin that a status surface shows (empty = none), sent once after initialize and again on every change
host_to_plugin.evaluate: request {query} -> {ok, answers}; CPU-only over pre-warmed state
host_to_plugin.hints: request {bundle_id, pid, front_window_frame, display_scale? (physical pixels per AppKit point)} -> {ok, targets, context_pid?}; always live
host_to_plugin.text_grid: request {bundle_id, pid, front_window_frame, display_scale? (physical pixels per AppKit point)} -> {ok, columns, rows, lines}; always live; sent to the focused app's hint providers in hint order, first non-empty grid wins; each line is one text_grid_line shape; empty lines = no grid
host_to_plugin.perform: request {kind: resolve|command|navigate, ...} -> {ok, target_pid?, navigation_url?, message?} | {ok:false, unhandled:true} | {ok:false, error}; a command is one perform_command shape: a core command the manifest declares under one of Flash's topics (with context), the plugin's own command or a bang (without)

plugin_to_host_notifications.publish: {rows, source?} — the plugin's catalog, host-owned store. Without `source`: a full replacement of every source's rows. With `source` (a manifest sources[].name that every row carries): a replacement of that source's rows alone, the other sources keeping theirs — a publish stays proportional to the change when volatile and static rows are separate sources. Quotas apply to the whole catalog after the merge; empty rows = authoritative empty (of the catalog, or of that source); transient failure = don't publish (host keeps last-good). The host decodes publishes on a queue that carries no replies, so a publish and a later reply are not ordered host-side; publishes of one plugin keep their order.
plugin_to_host_notifications.status: {segments: {name: value}} — manifest-declared names only; value is markup ("" clears) or a carousel object {prefix?: markup, lines: [markup], cycle_seconds: >= 1} the host rotates on its own clock (no lines clears; malformed objects are rejected whole)
plugin_to_host_notifications.poll: {registrations: {name: {every: seconds, priority} | {after: seconds, priority}}} — full-replacement set of the cadences (`every`) and one-shot deadlines (`after`, measured from receipt) the host should drive for this plugin; empty clears. Plugins must not arm their own timers or sleep to schedule work: the host folds every registration in the app onto one clock and sends `event {name: "core:poll:<name>"}` when one is due, regardless of manifest `listen`. A deadline fires once; repeating it unchanged in a later set neither re-arms nor re-fires it, and a changed or new name arms it afresh. Ticks are one-way and unacknowledged, so a plugin still running its previous callback drops the ones it missed instead of catching up. Bounds live in the `poll` section; a malformed or over-bound frame is rejected whole.
plugin_to_host_notifications.log: {level, message, fields, trace?} — content-free; trace names the interaction of the request being served

host_events.$comment: Every `core:*` event the host delivers through `event`, gated by manifest `listen`. `replacement` kinds are state signals: each supersedes the earlier ones with the same coalescing key, the event name plus, for core:ax.changed, the payload pid and notification. While a replacement frame waits unsent in the host's outbound queue, a newer one with the same key drops it and joins the tail, so a child reads a subsequence of the emitted events in emission order; requests, responses and other events stay FIFO under the transport budget. Under backlog the plugin likewise keeps only the latest of each key. core:apps.changed (payload {running_applications: [{bundle_id, pid, localized_name}]}) carries the complete snapshot of running regular apps. core:window.focus.changed (payload {pid, bundle_id}) names the app whose focused or main window changed. core:ax.changed (payload {pid, notification, bundle_id?}; both pid and a non-empty notification are required) reports one AX notification an observed app posted, one of `ax_notifications`: the value change of each keystroke is AXValueChanged, so match the notification instead of debouncing every change alike. core:network.changed (network interfaces, addresses, routes or DNS changed; payload {}) and core:volumes.changed (a volume mounted, unmounted or was renamed; payload {}) are payload-free, coalesced signals whose monitors run only while a plugin listens: re-read what you need. core:system.slept and core:system.woke bracket a system sleep, core:displays.slept and core:displays.woke a display sleep, core:screen.locked and core:screen.unlocked the lock screen; all payload {}. core:displays.changed (payload {added: [name], removed: [name], displays: [name]}) reports a display connected or removed. core:space.changed (payload {}) follows the active Space. core:user.idle (payload {seconds}) reports that nobody touched the keyboard, mouse or trackpad for one of the subscribers' idle thresholds (300 s for a plugin), once per away episode and threshold; core:user.active (payload {idle_seconds}) follows when input comes back after an announced episode. core:usb.attached and core:usb.detached (payload {vendor_id?, product_id?, name?}, never a serial number) report a USB device connected or removed; devices already connected are not announced. core:clock.minute (payload {time: "HH:MM", weekday: "mon"…"sun", date: "YYYY-MM-DD", late_seconds}, in the local time zone) reports that a wall-clock minute began; a plugin listener hears every minute. After a sleep or a locked screen it hears only the current minute, with how late it is. core:workspace.changed (payload {workspace, previous?, workspaces: [name]}) follows the focused tiling workspace while [tiling] is on. core:mode.changed (payload {mode, previous, layer?}: normal, insert, command, terminal, hyper, hold, visual, layer or disabled; layer names the active layer) follows Flash's mode. core:hints.shown (payload {surface, targets}) reports a hint session's first labels on screen, core:hints.committed (payload {surface}) each target it commits and core:hints.cancelled (payload {surface}) a session that ended without committing; never which target, its text or its label. core:monitor.triggered (payload {monitor, level: warning|error}) reports a value monitor rising into warning or error; never the value. Every event but core:apps.changed, core:ax.changed, core:session.opened and core:status.observed, the plugin plumbing, also reaches the clients of the resident's socket that subscribe to it (docs/ipc-protocol.md).

poll.$comment: Bounds of a `poll` registration set. priority sets the slack the shared clock may add to a wake-up so unrelated ones coalesce (high 25 ms: a value on screen the user watches change; normal 100 ms: ordinary sampling and settles; low 1 s: background upkeep, remote pulls, retries). The core-only `system` priority is not available to plugins. every is floored at min_every_ms; every and after are capped at max_seconds; a set holds at most max_registrations names of 1..max_name_bytes characters from [a-z0-9_-].

applescript.$comment: Typed host-owned AppleScript templates; no source code, script field, raw terminology or evaluated strings are accepted. Requests carry operation, timeout_ms and the operation-specific data fields. All strings enter templates only as escaped literals. Supported browser IDs use fixed Chromium/Safari dialects. Every operation checks its actual target against manifest apple_events_targets; shortcuts use com.apple.shortcuts.events and chat_submit uses com.apple.systemevents. The plugin needs apple_events. script_bytes bounds generated source; result_bytes bounds the UTF-8 result; deadlines and per-plugin concurrency include queue admission. The host returns {ok:true,result} or {ok:false,error,status?}; source/results never enter diagnostics.

publish.$comment: The publish notification's params: `rows` always; `source` names the one manifest sources[].name whose rows these replace (every row must carry it), absent for a whole-catalog replacement. Any other key rejects the publish whole.

perform_command.$comment: The perform {kind: command} shape. command and subcommand are the two words (a bang: the plugin id and the token); args are the argument words as a mapping writes them (--index=3, --force, or a bang's query words). context is the focused app and is present exactly for a core command the manifest's commands[] declares under one of Flash's topics, never for a plugin's own command or a bang.

row.$comment: Catalog row shape for publish. `source` is first-class and must name a manifest sources[].name; routing source_id stays host-stamped and never crosses the wire.

lifecycle.$comment: The manifest `lifecycle` key. Absent, the surfaces decide (resident, on-demand, status-bound; see docs/plugin-protocol.md Activation). `publish_then_exit` is a catalog-only plugin: `exec` and `sources`, none of the surfaces a live child serves (`forbids`). Its run is `on_start`: it publishes its catalog and exits 0 on its own, and the host keeps the catalog, reports the plugin as `published`, counts that exit as success (no restart, no failure budget) and answers its performs `unhandled` (its rows carry host effects). A non-zero exit or a signal is still a crash. The host runs it again when its `[plugins.<id>]` settings change, when a file named by one of its `watch_settings` changes (`watch_settings` lists setting names whose string value is a path: `~` expands to the home, a relative path is under the plugin root; the key needs this lifecycle), on `plugins reload`, and when its own files change. Such a plugin receives no events, the running-apps snapshot included.

source_types.$comment: Every manifest sources[] entry declares one `type`, the one word users filter the flashlight by (`@tabs`). A type matches `pattern`. `core` types are fed by Flash alone; a plugin declaring one fails to load. A `shared` type fixes the `kind` every source of it declares. Any other matching word is a new type, and every plugin declaring it must agree on its kind. The plugin! macro checks each manifest against this table at build time; the host checks again at load.

hint_target.$comment: The host revalidates geometry and target identity before clicking. context_id is an optional non-empty opaque string identifying the containing live source context; a changed context cancels the captured target. Omitted or null means unspecified.

text_grid_line.$comment: The two exact key sets of a text_grid line; rows and columns are cells, row 0 at the top, row < rows and column < columns. text is captured cell text, one UTF-16 unit per cell from column on (a terminal capture's addressing). format is an expanded tmux status format the host lays out across width >= 1 cells (column + width <= columns) with its status-line rules; style markers are not text and a blank layout is dropped. One malformed line rejects the whole reply.

effects.$comment: Closed union. copy_text/insert_text everywhere; open on rows only (answers cannot manufacture navigation). There is deliberately no run effect — argv side effects belong in perform, inside the sandbox.

quotas.$comment: Atomic rejection doctrine: any violation rejects the complete payload (a publish keeps the previous catalog; a reply serves empty); nothing is ever truncated. catalog_rows and catalog_bytes bound the plugin's whole catalog after a per-source merge. catalog_bytes counts the `rows` array as written on the wire — each row object's span in the publish frame, one separator byte per row and the two brackets — measured by the host from the frame it received, never by re-encoding: the compact encoding is the floor, and a plugin pays for whitespace or escaping it adds inside a row (the Rust SDK writes compact rows, so its count is the compact encoding exactly). answers_bytes counts the compact encoding of `answers`.

errors.$comment: Canonical EXACT protocol-level error strings (spec-pinned; domain failures stay free-form and content-free). The response law: every result carries boolean `ok`; ok:false carries a non-empty `error` — except perform's {ok:false, unhandled:true} (not mine; host MAY fall back). A perform {ok:false, error} means mine-but-broke: the host MUST NOT fall back.
errors.protocol_mismatch: protocol version mismatch: host v<H>, plugin v1
errors.initialize_repeated: initialize may only be called once

id_semantics: positive monotonic integers per sender; host and plugin counters are independent and may overlap (an inbound id+method frame is always a request). Exactly one reply per id'd request. Responses to unknown ids are dropped silently. There is no cancellation: late replies are dropped and the deadline table is the contract.

trace.host_to_plugin: optional `trace` key on a request envelope (hints, text_grid, evaluate, perform) naming the user interaction that caused it
trace.plugin_to_host: a `log` notification emitted while serving that request carries it back as params.trace; a malformed id is ignored

deadline.host_to_plugin: optional `deadline_ms` on a request envelope: the milliseconds the host still waits for the reply as it writes the request, a positive integer
deadline.plugin: a hints or text_grid handler still running a tenth of the deadline (at most 50 ms) before it is dropped and answers errors.deadline_exceeded; evaluate and perform run to completion

encoding: UTF-8 JSON, one object per newline-terminated line both directions; geometry in NSScreen coordinates; undecodable or oversized lines are dropped (never fatal), the stream self-heals at the next newline; EOF discards an unterminated record before shutdown

transport_limits.$comment: Per-process admission bounds. Plugin replacement-event overflow retains one latest slot per coalescing key (host_events) in addition to the ordinary event backlog, at most plugin_replacement_slots keys at once; each slot obeys frame_bytes, and a new key beyond the bound is dropped like an overflowing ordinary event. A full synchronous control reply queue closes the transport rather than blocking the stdin reader.
